hand_derivations.probability: Four equiprobable cards, three labelled cat: P(cat)=3/4=.75, P(dog)=1/4=.25, sum=1. Two independent .5 successes: .5*.5=.25.
hand_derivations.logs: If p=e^a, ln(p)=a; e≈2.718281828 and e^-1≈.367879441. ln(ab)=ln(a)+ln(b) for a,b>0; -ln(p)≥0 for 0<p≤1, derivative -1/p<0, limit +∞ as p→0+. Values at .9/.5/.1/.25 round to .105/.693/2.303/1.386. Equality of rounded .693+.693 and 1.386 is only display rounding, while the unrounded identity is exact over positive reals.
hand_derivations.matmul: For R=[[2,1,0],[1,2,1]], W=[[10,0],[20,1],[30,4]], RW=[[40,1],[80,6]]. Each output(i,j)=sum_k R(i,k)W(k,j), so it mixes materials within a recipe, not recipes with each other. Bias [5,0] gives [[45,1],[85,6]], [8,0] gives [[48,1],[88,6]].
hand_derivations.derivative: L(w)=(w-3)^2. Difference quotient [L(w+h)-L(w)]/h=2(w-3)+h. At w=1 this tends to -4; h=.1 gives -3.9 and the loss change -.39. A .1 step uses w_new=1-.1*(-4)=1.4; L_new=2.56 and L_prime=-3.2. With lr=.6: w_new=3.4 and L=.16. With lr=1.1: w_new=5.4 and L=5.76. This quadratic shows a correctly signed gradient can still worsen loss with an excessive step; it does not promise all objectives or rates improve.
hand_derivations.bit_packing: 3<<4=48=0b110000; OR 5 gives 53=0b110101; 53>>4=3 and 53&15=5. The two values in this example fit in four bits; no signed or overflow behavior is claimed.
